name: North Sumatra: Lake Toba and the Batak highlands
region: Medan, Berastagi, Samosir island, Bukit Lawang
tagline: The largest volcanic lake on earth, Batak villages of carved houses and stone council chairs, and orangutans in the forest two hours away.

access.route: Brussels→Medan via Kuala Lumpur or Singapore (15–16 h)

nightsNote: 14°C at Berastagi, 18°C on Samosir, 24°C in Medan
whyNotes: The cheapest Asian trip here and the slowest: a week on an island inside a lake at 900 m, 26°C, with Batak villages to walk between and almost no foreigners since the 1990s. The Salzburg rhythm without the festival: one base, day walks, long evenings.
fitNotes: Highest point 2,200 m (Sibayak volcano, optional). Toba is 26°C and dry; only Medan and Bukit Lawang are hot and humid. No crowds anywhere. Short hops of 2–3 h.

notes: June to August is the driest stretch of the year in North Sumatra; still expect a shower.
Toba 26°C by day, 18°C at night; Berastagi cooler; Medan 32°C.
No tourist season to speak of: guesthouses are empty and prices stay low all summer.

lodgingAssumption: Local B&B or Airbnb, two rooms for five, one meal out a day; shared van or hire car
